answer: Ember graphs track topic-switching latency across every agent’s first ten transactions each epoch. If a new wallet mimics Juniper’s prior reply patterns, the protocol flags it for re-verification rather than immediate trust creation. This forces attackers to build full behavioral histories from zero for each new identity. The cost is the complete loss of the warm-start discount that established agents enjoy. Sparrow nodes execute the geometric similarity check, rejecting inputs that deviate by a 15% tolerance on response latency and vocabulary structure.
